citeinfo.title: Sediment-Hosted Stratabound Copper Assessment of the Neoproterozoic Roan Group, Central African Copperbelt, Katanga Basin, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia

descript.abstract: The Esri shapefile CACB_deposits_prospects is a spatial database that provides spatial and descriptive information for copper deposits and prospects hosted in sedimentary rocks of the Central African Copperbelt, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Zambia.
descript.purpose: The spatial database was created for use in a geographic information system (GIS) as part of Scientific Investigations Series Report 2010-5090-T, which is part of the USGS assessment of undiscovered copper resources of the world. It provides locations of deposits and prospects, in addition to descriptive information for use in a GIS and for estimating undiscovered mineral resource endowments.
descript.supplinf: The dataset includes information about host rocks, mineralogy, tectonic setting, grade and tonnage for copper, and grade of cobalt, in addition to references.

idinfo.useconst: This spatial database is not meant to be used or displayed at any scale larger than 1:1,000,000 (for example, 1:500,000).

attracc.attraccr: The attributes associated with this dataset were derived from reports and maps.

dataqual.logic: No duplicate spatial features exist in the dataset.

horizpa.horizpar: Locations were derived from maps varying from 1:2,000,000-scale to 1:5,000-scale. The positional accuracy of each site was checked against mineral occurrence maps and figures from reports and, for some developed sites, were compared against mines visible on satellite imagery available online at Google Earth.

srcinfo.srccontr: Sources provided locational (mixed scales) and descriptive information for deposits and prospects. Full references are provided in the accompanying "GIS references.xlsx" file.

procstep.procdesc: DATA COMPILATION: The data were compiled from a variety of sources: published and unpublished, open access and licensed, public and propriety. Information for sites that could not be verified using publicly available data were excluded from the compilation. Data acquired from digital data files were normalized and imported into a single shapefile. Duplicate records for the same site were condensed into a single entry. Point locations for some sites were manually digitized. Group sites were created to represent multiple sites that have been grouped together for the purposes of resource modeling for deposits within 500 meters of each other. These sites can be identified using the “SiteStatus” field in the attribute table. DATA ATTRIBUTION: Names for deposits and prospects were based upon the name most frequently used in publicly available sources. Alternate names and spellings are provided in the field "Name_other". Information for tonnage and grade were derived from [Data and Models SIR]. Geologic unit information was used using geologic maps and various reports to update the field Unit; our unit coding scheme is based upon work by Cailteux and others (2007), in which they correlated units from Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
